features.description: Terminal-native coding agent with first-class support on macOS, Linux, Windows (PowerShell/WSL), Android, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, and NetBSD.
Choose from a wide range of LLMs or add your own via OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible APIs, Charm's hosted Hyper models, or the Catwalk community registry.
Switch LLMs mid-session while preserving context.
Maintain multiple saved work sessions and contexts per project.
Uses language servers for additional context, like an IDE does.
http, stdio, and SSE MCP servers with OAuth (including pre-registered clients) and per-server timeout, env, and disabled-tools options.
Auto-approve specific tools with `permissions allow` rules in the config.
Broad auto-approve mode that still blocks dangerous commands.
Introduced in v0.95.0 ('Hello, Plan Mode'); plan/normal mode badges shown in the TUI.
On-demand skill files, toggleable on/off from the command palette (v0.101.0).
User-defined scripts (any executable) triggered on agent lifecycle events such as PreToolUse, receiving JSON on stdin.
Built-in config skill lets you configure Crush by asking; crushrc and JSON config files with a published schema.
Homebrew, npm, winget, scoop, nix, Arch, and FreeBSD packages.
Free and open-source; you bring your own models/keys, with Charm's hosted Hyper models as the quick-start default.
